instruction:
FIX-ROUND R2 for slice 020b1 (WP-SCP-020 §4 020B.1).

R2 review surfaced 5 CRIT+MAJ findings to close. Read scope_boundary files + spec_paths first.

## Findings to close (sanitized)

### COR-R2-001 [MAJ, lens=correctness]
**Claim:** The reusable-workflow pins in workflow-selftest.yml are pegged to 76e0f0d8a744785b7fb2adb1b9e63c13757f2ae2 (the R1 evidence commit), but the current branch HEAD is f2a674b (the fix-round commit that modified policy-check.yml by adding the fixture-path input). The self-enforcing preflight will detect this stale-pin condition when the PR is submitted and fail with 'policy-check.yml changed in this PR; update both workflow-selftest pins to {head}', blocking merge. Even if the preflight is bypassed, the fixture-pass and fixture-fail jobs call policy-check.yml@76e0f0d which does not declare fixture-path; GitHub Actions would reject the call with an undeclared-input error.
**Evidence:** workflow-selftest.yml lines 91 and 187: uses: ./.github/workflows/policy-check.yml@76e0f0d8a744785b7fb2adb1b9e63c13757f2ae2. dispatcher-result.json git_sha_before == git_sha_after == 76e0f0d8a744785b7fb2adb1b9e63c13757f2ae2 (dispatcher ran from 76e0f0d and did not commit). files_changed_self_report in dispatcher-result.json includes .github/workflows/policy-check.yml (change_type: modified). Commit f2a674b ('Slice 020B.1 fix-round R1: close 8 R1 CRIT+MAJ findings') committed these modifications. policy-check.yml at 76e0f0d does not include fixture-path in workflow_call.inputs (that input was added in f2a674b). validate-selftest-config preflight: 'if ".github/workflows/policy-check.yml" in changed and pins[0] != head: raise SystemExit(...)' (workflow-selftest.yml lines 54-57). When the PR is submitted, head = full SHA of f2a674b != 76e0f0d8a744785b7fb2adb1b9e63c13757f2ae2, so preflight fires.
**Impact:** The selftest workflow self-blocks: its own CI gate will fail for this PR because the preflight enforces pins == head whenever policy-check.yml changed, and that condition is met. Additionally, at runtime the reusable-workflow call at @76e0f0d would error because the callee at that commit does not declare fixture-path while the caller passes it. Neither failure is a design flaw — both are correct enforcement — but the committed state is inconsistent and requires one more commit to advance the pins to the full SHA of f2a674b before the branch can merge.
**Mitigation:** Update both occurrences of the SHA in workflow-selftest.yml (lines 91 and 187) and both PIN comments (lines 89 and 185) from 76e0f0d8a744785b7fb2adb1b9e63c13757f2ae2 to the full 40-character SHA of the current branch HEAD (commit f2a674b). Obtain the full SHA via git rev-parse HEAD before committing. The preflight verify command in the fix-round dispatch-package (verify_commands[2]) will confirm the two pins are equal and both are 40-char hex after the update.

### R2-SBP-MAJ-01 [MAJ, lens=safety]
**Claim:** The fixture-path isolation fix resolves the scoping problem but introduces a new exit-code chain break: after 020C lands Rego rules, fixture-fail-policy-check will invoke policy-check.yml with default threshold: deny, exit 1 on the deliberately-violating services.yml, and workflow-selftest (which has needs: [stash-fixture-pass-summary, fixture-fail-policy-check] with no if: always()) will be SKIPPED — the comparison step for fixture-fail will never execute. The 020C transition remains non-viable.
**Evidence:** workflow-selftest.yml:179–188: fixture-fail-policy-check job passes fixture-path: tests/workflow/fixture-fail with no threshold: override; policy-check.yml:14 default threshold='deny'; policy-check.yml:419–422: if effective_denies and os.environ.get('SCP_THRESHOLD')=='deny': sys.exit(1). workflow-selftest.yml:190–196: workflow-selftest job declares needs: [stash-fixture-pass-summary, fixture-fail-policy-check] with no if: always() guard. GitHub Actions: a dependent job is SKIPPED when any needs-job fails. After 020C, fixture-fail/services.yml carries mode.bearer_legacy without valid deprecation date (tests/workflow/fixture-fail/services.yml:14–16) which SCP-R-001 will deny. fixture-fail-policy-check exits 1; workflow-selftest is skipped; the comparison step that asserts fixture-fail's deny findings match the oracle file never runs.
**Impact:** The structural guarantee that fixture-fail produces the EXPECTED deny finding (as recorded in the oracle) is never asserted after 020C. The selftest only confirms that the workflow exited 1 (blocked), not WHICH rule triggered or WHAT finding was recorded. An adversary can modify Rego rule output fields (rule_id, message, remediation_url) or the bypass_emitted flag without the oracle comparison catching it. The CG-CRIT-01 closure report from fix-round-1 is premature: scoping is fixed, but the comparison chain is still broken after 020C.
**Mitigation:** Option A — add threshold: warn to both fixture invocations in workflow-selftest.yml; the job exits 0 even with deny findings, the comparison chain completes, and the oracle comparison asserts the correct deny output. A separate step (or the comparison step itself) asserts that fixture-fail's actual findings array contains at least one deny-verdict entry. Option B — add if: always() to the workflow-selftest job and change its needs: to use needs.fixture-fail-policy-check.result == 'failure' || needs.fixture-fail-policy-check.result == 'success' logic; this is fragile in GitHub Actions YAML. Option A is cleaner. Must be implemented before 020C opens.

### R2-SBP-MAJ-02 [MAJ, lens=safety]
**Claim:** The selftest comparison validates summary JSON content but not threshold-enforcement exit behavior. An adversary can remove sys.exit(1) from the Render-deny-annotations step of policy-check.yml, update the SHA pin to satisfy the preflight check, and the selftest will not detect the removal: the comparison passes because findings still appear in the JSON summary, but the required-status check no longer blocks PRs on deny findings.
**Evidence:** policy-check.yml:419–422: the sole enforcement point is \`if effective_denies and os.environ.get('SCP_THRESHOLD')=='deny': sys.exit(1)\`. workflow-selftest.yml:220–268 (Compare reusable-workflow summaries): normalize() extracts schema_version, rule_set, findings, disabled_rules, waivers_applied, bypass_emitted, conflict_gate — no assertion on job exit code. If sys.exit(1) is removed, the workflow produces an identical summary (deny findings still recorded in JSON) and exits 0; fixture-fail-policy-check exits 0; workflow-selftest runs and compares; normalize(actual)==normalize(expected) passes. validate-selftest-config enforces that if policy-check.yml changed then pins==HEAD; the attacker satisfies this by updating both pins to their malicious commit HEAD. After 020K adds CODEOWNERS on .github/workflows/**, this attack requires a CODEOWNER approval, but in 020B.1 no CODEOWNERS exists.
**Impact:** After 020C adds Rego rules and 020D2 enables the required check, a PR that modifies policy-check.yml to remove threshold enforcement (removing six lines at policy-check.yml:419–422) while keeping summary JSON generation intact will pass the selftest and, subsequently, will cause scp/policy-check to always exit 0 — allowing any PR with any policy violation to merge. This is the highest-value attack on the primitive: it neutralizes the enforcement without altering the observability surface. The self-reported concern from R1 about this scenario remains unaddressed.
**Mitigation:** Add an explicit exit-code assertion to the selftest harness: after 020C, the fixture-fail-policy-check job (or a wrapper step around it) should be expected to exit 1, and workflow-selftest should assert the job outcome was 'failure'. Implementable by adding a step to workflow-selftest that reads the needs context: \`if [ '${{ needs.fixture-fail-policy-check.result }}' != 'failure' ]; then exit 1; fi\`. This requires workflow-selftest to have if: always() (see R2-SBP-MAJ-01). Alternatively, add a canary assertion in the comparison step: for the fixture-fail case, assert that actual['findings'] contains at least one entry with verdict=='deny' AND assert that a downstream wrapper invocation of policy-check.yml with the same fixture-fail input would exit non-zero — the latter requires a dedicated canary step. The combination of R2-SBP-MAJ-01 (if: always()) and this finding (exit-code assertion) must be addressed together.

### R2-CMP-MAJ-01 [MAJ, lens=completeness]
**Claim:** CG-MAJ-02 from R1 is not closed in the governance canonical: plan §4 020B.1 still lists only three trigger paths (.github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/**) and omits schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json. No tracked remediation item (BACKLOG row or future-slice requirement) exists to ensure the plan is ever amended.
**Evidence:** docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020B.1 row: 'SCP-local job workflow-selftest trigger = pull_request on paths .github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/** (blocks merge of any PR touching those paths).' — three paths only. .github/workflows/workflow-selftest.yml lines 5–9: paths: .github/workflows/policy-check.yml, policies/**, tests/workflow/**, schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json — four paths. Fix-round dispatcher-result.json self_reported_concerns: 'docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md was outside the allowed write scope, so the schema-trigger rationale was documented in the in-scope dispatch artifacts rather than in the parent plan row itself.' No BACKLOG.md entry, no future-slice reference in any committed plan document names this gap as requiring resolution.
**Impact:** The plan §4 020B.1 row is the governance canonical for 020B.1 conformance audits. Every subsequent reviewer comparing implementation to plan spec will find an undocumented trigger path. More critically: an implementor following only the plan to recreate or extend the selftest trigger set would omit schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json, creating a CI blind spot where schema changes bypass the selftest gate. The gap is live through all remaining WP-SCP-020 slices since no remediation is scheduled.
**Mitigation:** Amend plan §4 020B.1 trigger-path row to add schemas/policy-check-summary.schema.json with rationale '(expected-annotations.json is schema-bound; schema changes must re-validate all fixture expectations)'. This is a one-line documentation edit. It can be combined with the fixture-path input amendment required by R2-CMP-MAJ-02 into a single plan-amendment commit. Open a BACKLOG item or add a pre-dispatch requirement to 020C to confirm this edit lands before 020C review checkpoint.

### R2-CMP-MAJ-02 [MAJ, lens=completeness]
**Claim:** The fixture-path input added to policy-check.yml during fix-round R1 is not reflected in plan §4 020B AC (i) input enumeration. Plan §4 020B AC (i) is the canonical deliverable specification for the reusable workflow's input surface; it enumerates exactly six inputs. The implementation now has seven. No plan amendment was made and none is scheduled.
**Evidence:** docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md §4 020B AC (i): 'inputs: enumerated with type: — rule-set: string (default: "starter"), threshold: string (default: "deny"), annotate: boolean (default: true), scp_bypass: boolean (default: false), waivers-path: string (default: "output/findings/waivers.json"), rule-config-path: string (default: ".scp/rule-config.yaml").' Six inputs only. .github/workflows/policy-check.yml lines 6–40: seven inputs, including fixture-path: string (default: '.') at lines 37–40. Fix-round dispatch package scope_boundary excluded docs/plans/WP-SCP-020-policy-federation-primitive.md. Executor self_reported_concerns acknowledge the plan was out of write scope; no tracked remediation item exists. WP-SCP-020 §9 AC 6 ('workflow-selftest green on pass + fail fixtures') implicitly depends on fixture-path being present, but the AC text makes no mention of it.
**Impact:** A post-WP completeness audit comparing implementation to plan §4 020B AC (i) will flag fixture-path as undocumented scope. More critically, downstream adopters reading the plan for the canonical input surface will not see fixture-path and may not know it exists. Adopters who want to scope policy evaluation to a subdirectory (a valid use case given the input's default-'.'-semantics) have no plan-level pointer to this capability.
**Mitigation:** Amend plan §4 020B AC (i) to add 'fixture-path: string (default: ".") — restricts changed-file discovery to a path prefix; defaults to whole-repo evaluation for normal callers; used by the selftest harness to achieve fixture-tree isolation.' This amendment can be batched with the R2-CMP-MAJ-01 trigger-path fix into a single plan edit commit before 020C opens.


## Acceptance
- Every CRIT and MAJ closed in code/plan as appropriate.
- Run verify_commands; report status=complete only when green.
- Don't quote finding-IDs verbatim in code/commit messages.
- D-021 reservation respected.
